questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.**

You can go to ______ National Art Gallery but I want to visit ______ zoo first.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'the; the'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• In the given sentence, the nouns 'National Art Gallery' and '**Zoo**' are specific or particular nouns.
 
• The article 'the' is a definite article used **before a specific or particular noun**.
 
• 'The' is a definite article which restricts the meaning of a noun to one specific thing.
 
• The indefinite article 'a' is grammatically and contextually incorrect as it is used before a general noun.

 

Hence, from the given options we can say that **option 2** fits suitably in the blanks.

Correct sentence__: *You can go to **the** National Art Gallery but I want to visit **the** zoo first*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• The definite article (the) is used before a noun to indicate that the identity of the noun is known to the reader.
 
• The indefinite article (a, an) is used before a noun that is general or when its identity is not known.

questions.question:
**Directions: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.**

There will probably be a lot of fishes in their nets, will there?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'will there'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is a tag question. We use tag questions to ask for confirmation.
 
• A positive statement takes a negative tag and a negative sentence takes a positive tag.
 
• The given sentence is a positive statement and therefore, the auxiliary verb (will) from the positive statement is repeated in the tag and changed to negative (won't).
 
• Therefore, the negative tag 'won't' should be used in place of the positive tag 'will'.

 

Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct Sentence__: *There will probably be a lot of fishes in their nets, **won't there**?*

questions.question: **Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 3.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **'is'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This sentence implies the presence of one **singular item** ("a 100m-long strip of a concrete white wall") amongst a group of items (the "18 houses and farms").
 
• Therefore, the **verb **should agree with the** singular noun** ("strip"), not the plural nouns ("houses and farms"). 
 
• The **subject **of the sentence is "a 100m-long strip of a concrete white wall," which is **singular**. Hence, the **verb **should also be **singular** to match the **subject **in number.
 
• The prepositional phrase "Among the 18 houses and farms" modifies the subject by specifying its location but does not affect the number of the subject. The verb agreement is solely based on the main subject.

Therefore, the correct answer is- **is**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The option **"are"** would be incorrect because it is a plural verb, which would not agree with the singular subject "a 100m-long strip of a concrete white wall."
 
• The option **"have"** is also incorrect because it changes the meaning of the sentence to imply possession, which is not the context here. The sentence describes the presence of the wall among the houses and farms, not possession.
 
• The option **"has" **while singular, is primarily used with the third person singular pronouns (he, she, it) or with singular nouns referring to individuals or entities capable of possession. In this context, where the sentence is stating existence rather than possession, "is" is the most appropriate verb.
